title: Quarterly playbook: prewarm strategy and responsive scaling for dedicated pools
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Objective: define and deliver a repeatable quarterly playbook to prewarm dedicated GPU pools and enable responsive, cost-aware scaling for customer pools. Scope includes prewarming heuristics (time-of-day, traffic forecasting), fast-path provisioning (warm pool handoff, burst lanes), autoscale guardrails to preserve SLAs and cost targets, and observability dashboards + runbook. Out of scope: deep kernel/kernel-scheduler changes not needed for this release; full cross-cloud placement optimization is deferred to Q3.

Why this matters: Customers running dedicated pools currently see cold-start latency spikes during predictable traffic windows and occasional throttling under bursty demand. Prewarming combined with smarter responsive scaling should reduce tail latency, improve P50/P95 SLOs, and reduce emergency manual interventions.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc with step-by-step prewarm recipes for pool sizes and workloads.
- Implementation plan for prewarm controller + policy config + telemetry.
- Canary plan and A/B experiment across 3 pilot customers.
- Dashboards for prewarm effectiveness, warm-pool utilization, and cost delta.
- Rollback criteria and emergency mitigation steps.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive prewarming reduces latency but increases steady-state cost; we'll use time-windowed prewarm + dynamic thresholds to balance.
- Conservative burst lanes limit overprovisioning but may still impact P95 for extreme spikes; plan includes prioritized request routing for critical customers.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published in Confluence with verified runbook steps
Prewarm controller prototype deployed to staging and passes integration tests
Canary on 3 pilot pools shows >=30% reduction in cold-start P95 latency without >12% increase in baseline cost
Dashboard surfaces prewarm success rate, warm-pool fill, and cost delta per pool
Rollback and emergency scale pathways documented and validated in a table-top exercise
